sma50.label: 50-day SMA trend
sma50.measures: Whether the latest close sits above or below the stock's own 50-day simple moving average.
sma50.verdict: Scored. Its edge kept the same sign in both halves of the history (+2.65 early, +0.67 late), so it survived the consistency check — but it is deliberately damped. Trend-following helps in trending stretches and hurts in choppy ones, and a fit to a single split wanted 18, which did not generalise.

supertrend.label: Supertrend(10,3)
supertrend.measures: The direction of the Supertrend indicator (ATR period 10, factor 3) on the latest bar — the same calculation the candlestick chart draws.
supertrend.verdict: Scored, and damped for the same reason as the 50-day SMA. Consistent sign in both halves (+2.16 early, +0.65 late), but it is a second trend measure and correlates with the first, so neither carries a large weight.

seasonalityMax.label: Monthly seasonality
seasonalityMax.measures: How this stock has historically performed in the current calendar month, versus the month before. The contribution scales with the average and is capped at the weight shown.
seasonalityMax.verdict: Scored at low weight. Positive in both halves (+3.18 early, +1.57 late), but this is the thinnest evidence in the model — most stocks have only two or three observations of any given calendar month, so the cap keeps it from dominating a blend.

minerviniPass.label: Minervini 7/7 pass
minerviniPass.measures: All seven criteria of the Minervini Trend Template passing at once: price above its 150- and 200-day SMAs, the 50-day above both, the 200-day rising, price above its 50-day, at least 25% above the 52-week low and within 25% of the 52-week high.
minerviniPass.verdict: Scored NEGATIVELY — the single most consequential finding of the backtest. A full 7/7 pass was followed by UNDERperformance in every period tested (excess return of -7.9, -6.4 and -8.4 at three different train/test splits). It was the only signal whose sign held at every split. The structure is textbook bullish; on this market and sample, the forward outcome was not.

minerviniDown.label: Minervini downtrend
minerviniDown.measures: Two or fewer of the seven Minervini criteria passing while price trades below both the 150- and 200-day SMAs.
minerviniDown.verdict: Not scored. Its edge was -0.28 in the earlier half and +0.93 in the later half — the sign flips with the split, so no stable effect could be demonstrated.

macd.label: MACD crossover
macd.measures: The MACD(12,26,9) line crossing its signal line on the most recent bar.
macd.verdict: Not scored. Measured +0.67 in the earlier half and -0.70 in the later half — it changes sign depending on where the history is cut, which is the signature of noise rather than edge.

hm.label: Hilega-Milega crossover
hm.measures: RSI(9) crossing its own WMA(21) — the custom signal the candlestick page shades in the background.
hm.verdict: Not scored. +0.75 early, -0.15 late; the sign does not survive a change of split.

sweep.label: Liquidity sweep
sweep.measures: Price wicking beyond the recent 20-day range extreme and then closing back inside it on the same bar — a stop-hunt reversal.
sweep.verdict: Not scored, and the most volatile of the rejected signals: -2.70 early against +0.22 late. It also fires rarely, so the sample behind either number is small.

srProximity.label: Support/resistance proximity
srProximity.measures: Price sitting within 3% of an automatically detected support or resistance cluster.
srProximity.verdict: Not scored. +0.63 early, -0.58 late. The levels are still used to place stoplosses and targets — they just do not predict direction.

valuationMax.label: DDM valuation
valuationMax.measures: Price against a Gordon Growth intrinsic value built from the stock's cash dividend (5% growth, 12% required return) — the same model the Screener uses.
valuationMax.verdict: Not scored, and excluded on principle rather than on measurement. data/dividends.json stores only today's dividend figures with no historical record, so testing it against past prices would let information from the future leak into the past. A weight this process cannot honestly validate is not shipped.

heikinAshi.label: Heikin-Ashi conviction
heikinAshi.measures: A Heikin-Ashi candle with no opposing wick — bullish with the low pinned to the open, or bearish with the high pinned to the open — reading full follow-through rather than just direction.
heikinAshi.verdict: Not scored, but not for the usual reason: it actually passed the cross-regime check (+0.32 early, +0.68 late, same sign both halves). It failed a harder test — adding it on top of the shipped weights made ranking quality worse in every one of four independent windows, and progressively worse the more weight it got. It fires on roughly half of all scored bars and tracks the same trend structure the 50-day SMA and Supertrend already score, so its edge in isolation looks like a third counting of that same trend rather than new information.

breakoutRetest.label: Breakout & retest
breakoutRetest.measures: Price closes decisively beyond a trailing 20-day range (a full candle close, not just a wick), then later pulls back to touch that broken level again. If the level holds, that touch is the signal — old resistance flipped to new support, or the mirror on the downside.
breakoutRetest.verdict: Not scored, and its edge is real and its own — unlike Heikin-Ashi, it does not just repeat an existing signal (it fires on a specific event, ~3% of bars, not half). It passed the cross-regime check even more strongly (+0.62 early, +1.12 late), but it fails the four-window test a different way: scoring it roughly doubled trade volume by pushing many borderline-score stocks over the conviction threshold, and that extra volume was lower quality — average P&L fell in every window, in one case flipping from +1.11% to -1.03%.

rsi.label: RSI(14) overbought/oversold
rsi.measures: RSI(14) crossing back above 30 from oversold, or back below 70 from overbought — the classic mean-reversion trigger, distinct from the RSI(9)-vs-its-own-average trend read Hilega-Milega already uses.
rsi.verdict: Not scored. It passed the cross-regime check (-0.70 early, -1.49 late, same sign both halves) — but INVERTED from the textbook reading: exiting oversold measured negative forward edge on this market, not a bounce. Even with the sign corrected, adding it made the four-window blend worse.

marubozu.label: Marubozu
marubozu.measures: A full-bodied candle with next to no wick on either end (open/close pinned to the day's low/high) — one-sided conviction, with buyers or sellers in control from open to close.
marubozu.verdict: Not scored, despite measuring the strongest two-half edge of any signal tested (+0.94 early, +2.93 late, same sign both halves — stronger than seasonality's). It still made the four-window blend worse; it held up best on the Buy side alone (3 of 4 windows), just not the full composite.

pinBar.label: Hammer / shooting star
pinBar.measures: A small body pinned to one end of the day's range with a long wick (at least 2x the body) on the other — a hammer (long lower wick) after a decline, or a shooting star (long upper wick) after a rise.
pinBar.verdict: Not scored. -0.40 early, +0.24 late — the sign flips with the split, the standard signature of noise rather than edge.

dojiReversal.label: Dragonfly / gravestone doji
dojiReversal.measures: A doji (open and close pinned together, tiny body) where nearly the whole range sits on one side — a dragonfly (long lower wick, open/close near the high) or a gravestone (long upper wick, open/close near the low).
dojiReversal.verdict: Not scored. -1.10 early, +1.63 late — a large swing that flips sign with the split, the most volatile of the rejected candlestick patterns.

harami.label: Harami
harami.measures: A small candle whose entire body sits inside the prior day's (larger) body — that prior move suddenly losing momentum. Direction comes from the prior candle's colour: a big up day followed by containment is the bearish setup, a big down day the bullish one.
harami.verdict: Not scored. It passed the cross-regime check with a remarkably stable edge (-0.59 in BOTH halves, identical) — but INVERTED from the textbook reading, the same pattern as RSI. Even inverted, it made the four-window blend worse.

volumeSurge.label: Volume surge
volumeSurge.measures: Today's volume running at least 1.5x its trailing 20-day average on an up or down day — real participation behind the move, the "how strong is this trend" read price alone can't give.
volumeSurge.verdict: Not scored. Same sign in both halves (+0.19 early, +0.04 late) but too weak in the later half to clear the noise floor — never even reached the four-window test.

orderBlock.label: Order block retest
orderBlock.measures: The last opposite-colour candle before an impulsive move (body ≥ 1 ATR) that breaks 10-bar structure becomes a supply/demand zone; the signal is price returning to that zone and holding, gated by the 200 EMA so only with-trend pullbacks fire — the TradingLab "smart money" setup as taught.
orderBlock.verdict: Not scored. -0.12 early, +0.37 late — the sign flips with the split, so even with the structure-break, impulse and trend filters all applied, the setup is indistinguishable from noise on this market.

emaRibbon.label: EMA ribbon (13/21/34/55)
emaRibbon.measures: The 13/21/34/55 EMA stack falling into full bullish or bearish order for the first time — an alignment event, not the ongoing state, so it fires sparsely at trend starts rather than throughout a trend.
emaRibbon.verdict: Not scored. Same sign in both halves (+0.28 early, +0.48 late) but under the noise floor in the earlier half — and what edge there is duplicates the trend information the 50-day SMA and Supertrend already score.

method.lookahead: None in price signals — every indicator is a causal series, verified against the live detectors by scripts/verify-engine-parity.js.
method.sameBar: When one bar contains both the stoploss and the target, the stoploss is counted as hit first, since daily bars do not record the intrabar path.
method.overlap: At most one open simulated trade per stock at a time, so a single move is not counted repeatedly.
method.excluded: The DDM valuation signal is unscored: data/dividends.json holds only current figures, so any historical test of it would be contaminated by lookahead.

caveats: Price history for the full universe starts 2024/07/28, and the model's longest warmup is 221 bars, so 90% of stocks are not scorable until 2022/07/07. Of 8174 simulated trades, 9464 were struck before that while the universe was still coming online — 11811 of those predate the universe entirely and come from just 367 stocks. Read this as roughly a 49.3-month test of the broad market, not a decade.

caveats: "Explorer" — same trailing 2-year window and weights as "Last 2 years" above, with target capped at a maximum 1:2.5 reward:risk AND 12% price move from entry (whichever binds tighter), PLUS a profit-lock ladder: once price moves 2.1% from entry towards target the stop ratchets to +2%, then 4.1%→+4%, 5.1%→+5% and so on up to 11.1%→+11%, and it also locks at each opposing support/resistance level as price crosses it. The stop only ever tightens. Trades against the position also exit early when a daily close breaks the nearest adverse support/resistance level between entry and the stop — including role-reversed levels (a broken support acting as resistance from below, and vice versa), which the placement logic deliberately ignores. A max-risk gate refuses any trade whose stop sits more than 30% from entry — the class of trade that risks huge drawdown for a capped 12% target contributed over a third of all losses while averaging near zero, and declining it outright lowered P&L volatility in every validation window. Every surviving stop is pulled in to at most 5% from entry — a risk-preference choice, not an edge improvement: a 5% stop sits inside ordinary daily noise, so it caps the intended loss per trade at the cost of whipsaw exits. That whipsaw cost is then refunded by how the stop is BOOKED: a stoploss only executes when a daily close finishes beyond it, filled at that close — an intrabar dip through the stop that recovers by the close no longer exits at all. This close-confirmation was the strongest single change ever measured on this variant, and the same trades simply exit better (trade count is unchanged): buy net average improved in all four validation windows (+1.09/+1.04/+3.41/+3.56 → +1.28/+1.11/+4.61/+3.83) with net-losing trades down in all four (190/11/15/6 → 159/9/10/4), and the capital-constrained replay improved at every position size in both test periods (full history at 5 positions: +272% → +385%; trailing 2 years: +85% → +102% with maximum drawdown LOWER, 14.0 → 11.2). The documented price is a longer loss tail: a day that closes through the stop fills at the close, which can sit well past the 5% level, so the average genuine losing stop deepens from about -5.8% to -7.1% and single losses beyond -5% are now routine rather than gap-only — the 5% figure bounds where the stop sits, not what a losing exit books. Fewer, deeper losses, materially higher account return: adopted as a deliberate trade-off. Finally, three same-day entry filters have to agree before a trade is taken at all: the signal day's own candle must confirm the direction (no buy unless that day closed green, no sell unless it closed red), that day must trade more volume than the day before it, and on buys its upper wick must be no longer than 40% of the day's range — a rally that got sold into does not count as confirmation. The candle and wick filters each improved the buy-side average in every one of the four validation windows, the wick filter most strongly and with a clean dose-response behind its threshold; the volume filter is a smaller, more mixed gain. All three read only the signal bar itself, which is why they behave differently from the multi-day trend gates tried and rejected against this model — there is no multi-day state to go stale or lag. A fifth entry filter is a momentum floor: a buy candidate must ALREADY be up at least 20% over the prior 30 trading days. This is the inverse of the intuitive rule, and the inversion is the finding — blocking entries that had already run was the worst-performing gate ever measured against this model, losing in all four validation windows at every threshold tried across 10-, 15- and 30-day lookbacks. P&L rises monotonically with prior extension instead: over 30 days, longs not yet up 20% average -0.39% while those already up 20%+ average +0.73%, and the same gradient holds on 12,005 non-fund trades. Flat candidates are the illiquid ones whose signals fire off stale history and go nowhere. The floor declines roughly 70% of long entries, which costs nothing in practice because the model already produces far more signals than a fixed capital base can hold — see the portfolio simulation. A sixth condition then applies to buys: the entry candle must leave a LOWER wick of at least 40% of its range, so the day's dip was bought back before the close. That is the opposite wick from the rejection filter above it — one refuses a rally that was sold into, this one requires a dip that was defended. It arrived from an observation about a losing SHORT and only works inverted: as a sell filter it wins one window in four, but on the buy side it beat the ungated config in all four (+0.50 / +0.38 / +2.26 / +2.75 net against +0.28 / +0.05 / +0.62 / +0.93), and in the capital-constrained replay the portfolio moves from -1.7% to +36.1% at five concurrent positions with maximum drawdown cut from 23% to 12.6%. A seventh condition narrows the wick rule for stretched entries: a long sitting more than 20% above its own 20-day moving average is held to a 20% upper-wick ceiling rather than 40%, because an entry far from its mean has less room to absorb a rejection. The group it removes earned nothing — on the 2-year window those trades never once reached target, lost half the time, and returned -0.03% net against +3.57% for extended longs with a shorter wick. Two caveats: its bucket table is U-shaped rather than sloped, so the mechanism is less cleanly understood than the momentum floor's, and the model now fires roughly a hundred times a year at 9-22% average exposure — most of the capital sits in cash. An eighth condition applies to Mutual Fund buys only: the last COMPLETED week's candle must have closed green AND that week must have out-traded the week before it. Fund units are NAV-anchored and thinly traded, so a momentum signal without weekly participation behind it is usually stale-history noise — the same mechanism as the momentum floor's original mutual-fund finding. This is deliberately sector-scoped: the SAME pair of weekly rules was tested market-wide and REJECTED (per-trade it went 3-of-4 windows, but the capital-constrained replay showed it starving an under-deployed book — refused trades were refused return). Scoped to funds it removes only ~3% of the book, the trades it removes were net losers (fund slice +0.36% → +0.77% net, losing trades 25 → 17 across the full history), and the same replay that rejected the market-wide version improves at every position size with this scoping (5/10/15 positions: 265.9% → 272.3%, 119.5% → 122.2%, 74.9% → 76.2%, with maximum drawdown lower at 10 and 15). Honest caveat: the fund sector was singled out because the sector table flagged it, a post-hoc selection risk mitigated by the independent liquidity mechanism and the every-size replay margin, and two of the four validation windows contain only 1-2 fund trades so they contribute no evidence either way. This variant's ORIGINAL promising figures did not survive realistic market mechanics: once the simulation enforces DSE settlement (bought shares cannot be sold before T+2, or T+3 for Z-category stocks) and fills a stop at the OPEN when price gaps past it overnight, the ladder's tightly-spaced profit locks stop capturing the prices they assume — most "locked" exits really fill at the next open — and the variant went negative on this window while the shipped plan's level-backed stops barely moved. The momentum floor added afterwards is what recovered it: with settlement and gap fills still fully enforced, the long book is now net-positive after the 0.8% round-trip cost in all four validation windows, and the capital-constrained portfolio replay swings from roughly -33% to +18% over the trailing two years at 15 concurrent positions, with maximum drawdown cut from 38% to 11%. The figures below are the honest, settlement-aware numbers throughout. The sell side is untouched by any of this and remains negative — it is unreachable anyway, since DSE offers no short mechanism, so judge this variant on its Buy figures.
